judgment.detail: line 28 asserts 'OPI combines elements of both value function iteration and policy iteration' and then never says how - the reader is sent off-site to DP1 at line 30, and the algorithm box at 249-252 only lists the two steps. The missing connection is the one the whole lecture turns on: $m = 1$ is exactly VFI and $m \to \infty$ is policy iteration, so $m$ interpolates between them. It is never stated, even though the sweep at 387 includes $m=1$ and the summary at 416-417 relies on the large-$m$ end of that same idea. Separately, the exercise at 427 asks the reader to vary '$\rho$ and $\nu$' - symbols that appear nowhere in the lecture's narrative or math; they exist only as keyword arguments at line 95, because the income process itself was left in {doc}`ifp_discrete`

line 124 writes `a, y, ap  = a_grid[i], y_grid[j], a_grid[ip]` with two spaces before the `=` (pycodestyle E221); the parallel unpacking at line 177 in `T_σ` has one. The multi-space alignment at 133-135 and 194-195 is a different case and should be left alone - the aligned `in_axes` tuples make the moving axis read as a diagonal, which is the 'closer to mathematical notation' exception the rule allows for

strengths: The vectorization is built up one axis at a time (133-135) from a single scalar `B` at 114, with the `in_axes` tuples column-aligned so the axis being mapped reads down the diagonal - a reader can see what each `vmap` adds instead of facing one opaque call

`B`'s docstring at 116-121 writes the Bellman right-hand side out in ASCII and then pins the index convention, `(i, j, ip) -> (a, y, a')`, so every indexed expression in `T`, `get_greedy` and `T_σ` can be read straight back to the display at 166

Both solvers are timed twice with the first run labelled as including compile time (305-309, then 312 and 315-319; the same again at 325-341) - the right protocol for JIT-compiled code, and the prose says why rather than leaving the reader to wonder about the two numbers
Equivalence of VFI and OPI is checked rather than asserted: `jnp.allclose(v_star_vfi, v_star_opi)` at 346, then a side-by-side policy plot at 353-374 with the 45-degree line drawn in for reference

The $m$-sweep at 387-397 spans 1 to 400 and the resulting figure at 402-404 draws `vfi_time` as a horizontal reference line, so the crossover and the degradation at large $m$ are both readable off the plot rather than only stated in the bullets at 414-417

scanner_doubts: ifp_opi.md, line 102 - the 2 `qe-code-002` hits are false positives, and of the same kind as the `beta` hits in career.md. Line 102 is `mc = qe.tauchen(n=y_size, rho=ρ, sigma=ν)`: `rho` and `sigma` are the keyword-parameter names of the `quantecon.tauchen` function, not identifiers the author chose. The author's own variables ARE Unicode - they are the values being passed, `ρ` and `ν`, declared at line 95. Renaming the keywords would break the call. The check should skip identifiers in keyword-argument position (and names bound by an import), which would clear both this and the career.md case.

ifp_opi.md, line 30 - the 1 `qe-link-002` hit looks unactionable. The link is `[DP1](https://dp.quantecon.org)`. `dp.quantecon.org` is the *Dynamic Programming* book, not one of the five lecture series, and it is NOT in lecture-dp's `intersphinx_mapping`, which lists only `intro`, `intermediate` and `advanced` (lectures/_config.yml lines 96-105). There is no `{doc}` target to convert this to; doing what the rule asks would break the build. Either drop `dp.quantecon.org` from the known-intersphinx URL list, or the series needs the mapping added first.

Scope question affecting 5 of the 18 lecture-dp files I reviewed, not a miscount. The reports mark the JAX category 'out of scope' on the grounds that `qe-jax-*` targets `lecture-jax`, which is not in the corpus - but ifp_opi.md, ifp_discrete.md, ifp_egm.md, ifp_egm_transient_shocks.md and ifp_advanced.md all `import jax` and are written in exactly the idiom the JAX rules describe (`NamedTuple` model at 79-85 for qe-jax-002, `jax.lax.while_loop` / `fori_loop` at 215, 240, 286 for qe-jax-005, functional updates throughout for qe-jax-004). calvo_machine_learn.md also touches JAX. So 'out of scope' here is a statement about the repository the rules were written for, not about the lecture - and it silently exempts real JAX code from 7 rules. Worth deciding whether the JAX category should key off `import jax` in the file rather than off the series name.
